title: Integrability and bound for correlated Gaussian functions
statement:
Let $n$ be a natural number, and let $r,s,\rho\in\mathbb R$ satisfy $r>0$, $s>0$, $rs\le1$, $0\le\rho\le1$, and $\rho^2\le rs$. Suppose the two coordinate projections of the joint Gaussian law of $(X,\rho X+\sqrt{1-\rho^2}Y)$ each have standard Gaussian product measure as their distribution, for independent standard Gaussian vectors $X,Y\in\mathbb R^n$. If $f,g:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R$ belong respectively to $L^{1+r}(\gamma)$ and $L^{1+s}(\gamma)$, where $\gamma$ is standard Gaussian product measure, then $(x,y)\mapsto f(x)g(y)$ is integrable for the joint law, and
\[
\int |f(x)|\,|g(y)|\,d\mu_\rho(x,y)\le \|f\|_{1+r}\,\|g\|_{1+s},
\]
with the norms taken with respect to $\gamma$.
